concerns.text: FR-004 mandates a permutation test with 'a minimum of 1,000 iterations' using a 'model-seed null distribution (comparing cross-lingual similarity against same-language, different-seed similarities)'. However, the methodology only loads three specific models (Llama-3, Mistral, BLOOM) which are single instances. There is no mechanism defined in the spec to generate 'different-seed' variants of these models to create the required null distribution. The requirement contradicts the available data sources defined in US-1 and Assumptions.

SC-004 states the validation metric is measured against 'the correlation coefficient between the subspace orientation and external, non-LLM-derived typological features (e.g., WALS features)'. However, FR-006 only mandates acquiring 'Common Crawl subsets' and 'RedPajama lists'. There is no Functional Requirement to acquire, load, or process WALS features or any other external typological dataset. The success criteria references a data source and metric that the functional requirements do not support.

Inconsistent terminology: The story text refers to 'mean embedding' (centroid) and 'frequency distribution', but the acceptance scenario 1 mentions projecting the 'frequency distribution of the Common Crawl (French/Chinese) subset'. The spec does not explicitly define how the 'Common Crawl subset' maps to the 'frequency distribution' required for the projection, creating ambiguity in the data flow between the dataset acquisition (FR-006) and the projection logic (FR-005).

The Assumptions section states: 'The permutation test is computationally tractable on a standard multi-core CPU for [deferred] iterations'. This contradicts FR-004 which explicitly sets the minimum iteration count to '1,000'. The assumption defers a value that the requirement has already fixed, creating a logical conflict regarding the scope of the computational load.
